verdict.rationale: LobeHub's docs say each agent has persistent memory that the user can edit, which covers the inspect/edit core of the story. Chat data is stored client-side by default, but that is not explicitly said of the memory store, and no open storage format is documented. Markdown editing applies to agent profiles, not memory, so it does not count here. missing for 10: explicit memory deletion, confirmation that the memory store itself lives locally, a documented open format for memory, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, I can inspect, edit, and delete what the assistant has remembered — the memory store lives on my machine in an open format

citations.quote: Each agent has persistent memory, editable by you, allowing humans and agents to co-evolve over time.
LobeChat chat data is stored locally on the client-side by default.
